Taiwan.method: National ratio of withdrawals to renewable supply from Taiwan's Water Resources Agency (WRA), converted with Aqueduct's own scoring curve: raw = 16.37 / 63.37 = 0.258 (total water use / available runoff, 2013-2022 average); Aqueduct score = log2(raw/0.1)+1 = 2.37 (clamped 0-5; formula checked against Aqueduct 4.0 rows, e.g. raw 0.4268 -> 3.093); value = 2.37/5 = 0.474 (Aqueduct category 'Medium-high, 20-40%').
Taiwan.source: Water Resources Agency, MOEA (Taiwan), 'Water Resources Utilization': 10-yr avg rainfall 88.50 billion t; available runoff after evaporation and infiltration 63.37 billion t; average total water consumption 16.37 billion t (domestic 3.18, industrial 1.634, agricultural 11.55); groundwater pumping exceeds natural recharge. Average 2013-2022.

alternatives.method: Area-weighted Aqueduct 4.0 bws_score over all Taiwan admin-basin polygons (36,548 km2): 1.379/5. The main island is essentially one sub-basin (pfaf 437001, bws_raw 0.129, score 1.363 'Low-medium'); one small basin (437002, 154 km2) is 'Extremely high'.

alternatives.note: Taiwan is not named in WRI's 2015 2040-rankings article; the Aqueduct 3.0 ranking file sits behind a download form and could not be checked (Wayback was offline). Not used.

Taiwan.note: Aqueduct 4.0 has no Taiwan country score. The WRA-derived ratio is higher than the Aqueduct basin value because Aqueduct treats the whole island as one large basin. WRA 'available runoff' excludes infiltration while consumption includes groundwater, so the ratio may be slightly overstated. Neither measure captures Taiwan's strong wet/dry-season imbalance (the 2021 and 2023 droughts forced agricultural cuts); Aqueduct seasonal variability for basin 437001 is only 'Low-medium' (sev_score 1.49). Range 0.28-0.47; 0.474 recommended.

Singapore.method: WRI Aqueduct 2.1 country score of 5.00 (the maximum, 'extremely high') for Singapore -> 5/5 = 1.0. Supported by national data: demand ~440 mgd vs an import entitlement of up to 250 mgd from the Johor River (~57% of demand), i.e. withdrawals far exceed internal natural supply, which corresponds to Aqueduct raw >0.8 -> score 5.
Singapore.source: WRI (Maddocks, Young & Reig), 'Ranking the World's Most Water-Stressed Countries in 2040', 26 Aug 2015 - Singapore listed among 11 countries scoring 5.00/5 (business-as-usual 2040). Supporting: Singapore Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment water policy page (about 440 mgd demand; up to 250 mgd of raw water from the Johor River under the 1962 Water Agreement; demand to almost double by 2065).

alternatives.method: Aqueduct 4.0 basin value (pfaf 444055, shared with Johor, Malaysia): bws_raw 0.043 -> score 0
alternatives.note: Misleading: the basin includes Johor's supply and ignores Singapore's import dependence; WRI shows Singapore as 'NoData' at country level.

alternatives.method: UN SDG 6.4.2 (FAO) level of water stress
alternatives.source: UN SDG API series ER_H2O_STRESS, area 702
alternatives.note: FAO-estimated values swing from 309% (2000) to 58% (2019) to 7.04% (2022-23). They are unstable and exclude imports, NEWater and desalination, so they are not used.

Singapore.note: The 2015 score is for the 2040 business-as-usual projection (the article gives no separate current score). NEWater (reclaimed) and desalination reduce Singapore's physical supply risk, and AWS and Microsoft cool with NEWater, so 1.0 describes the scarcity of natural freshwater, not the risk of supply interruption.

caveats: WUE definitions differ: AWS reports on-site WUE per kWh of IT load for AWS-operated DCs (calendar year); Microsoft reports cooling+humidification water / IT kWh (fiscal year for fleet values; fact sheets give calendar 2021/2022 values or DESIGN values for sites 'not yet in operation'); Meta and derived ratios use total facility electricity.

Design/forecast values (Microsoft Mexico, Italy, Austria, Poland, Finland, Greece, Taiwan, New Zealand; also alternates for Brazil and Australia) are marked in 'scope'; operational WUE is often higher than design.

Several AWS country sheets print a regional fleet average instead of a country value (South Korea, Malaysia: AWS Asia Pacific 1.10; Switzerland, Italy: AWS Europe 0.05; USA primary: AWS North America 0.08). These are country-level proxies, not in-country measurements.
India/Thailand 0.0 come from AWS statements that no cooling water was used in 2025 (domestic water only); they reflect air-cooled hyperscale builds, not the local colocation market.
AWS WUE can swing sharply from year to year (Frankfurt 0.01 -> 0.17, Sao Paulo 0.23 -> 0.09); single-year values are noisy.

Google publishes per-site water consumption but not per-site electricity, so no Google site WUE could be derived. Equinix (0.95 all DCs, 1.55 evaporative-cooled DCs, 2024) and Meta (0.19, 2024) publish global fleet WUE only.

Regional fleet fallbacks for countries with null: AWS North America 0.08, AWS Europe 0.05, AWS Asia Pacific 1.10 (2025); Microsoft Global 0.27, Americas 0.34, APAC 0.25, EMEA 0.03 (FY25); Meta 0.19 (2024); Equinix 0.95 (2024).
The China value is a single operator's fleet average (GDS); the URL is the investor-relations landing page from earlier research, not a direct PDF link.
Water stress for Taiwan and Singapore is estimated (not an official Aqueduct country score); see the method fields.
